steps.title: Peel the lens shipping film
steps.detail: Some cameras might come with a small piece of translucent blue plastic film covering the lens. This is only present to protect the lens during shipping. To remove it, gently peel it off. (Raspberry Pi docs, Install a Raspberry Pi camera, Step 1.) If your camera has no film, skip this step.

troubleshoot.why: The Raspberry Pi docs describe a shipping film that covers the lens on some cameras.

cites.quote: Some cameras might come with a small piece of translucent blue plastic film covering the lens.

steps.title: Shut down and unplug the Pi
steps.detail: Shut down your Raspberry Pi and disconnect it from power. (Raspberry Pi docs, Step 2.) The docs also warn that cameras are sensitive to static: touch a sink tap or similar to earth yourself before handling the camera board.
warnings: Cameras are sensitive to static. Earth yourself prior to handling the PCB (docs warning).

troubleshoot.why: The docs install procedure starts with shutting down and disconnecting power.

cites.loc: Step 2. Connect the cable to your Raspberry Pi
cites.quote: Shut down your Raspberry Pi and disconnect it from power.

steps.title: Connect the camera cable
steps.detail: Follow the official Raspberry Pi page 'Install a Raspberry Pi camera' (Steps 2 and 3) for your exact Pi model and camera: which connector, which cable, how the flap opens and which way the contacts face. GhostBuild does not repeat those details because they differ by model. Your camera usually ships with the cable already attached. The same docs say the cable goes in the camera connector, not a display connector.
warnings: Do not bend the flexible cable at a sharp angle (docs).
Keep the Pi powered off until the cable is seated.

faq.q: which port does the camera use
which way do the contacts face

troubleshoot.why: The docs list a firmly seated, fully inserted, evenly inserted cable first.

cites.quote: Check that the FFC (Flat Flexible Cable) is firmly seated, fully inserted, and that the contacts face the correct direction.

troubleshoot.why: The docs say the cable fits either port but only the CSI port powers and controls the camera.

cites.quote: The connector fits into either port, but only the CSI port powers and controls the camera.

steps.title: Power the Pi back on
steps.detail: Reconnect your Raspberry Pi device to power and turn it on. (Raspberry Pi docs, Step 4.) Then make sure your software is up to date and install rpicam-apps as the docs describe. Start the GhostBuild Pi service as written in pi/README.md.

faq.q: do i need to update software

troubleshoot.why: The docs say the camera adds about 200-250mA and a low quality supply may not power it.

cites.quote: The Camera Module adds about 200-250mA to the power requirements of your Raspberry Pi.

steps.title: Camera feed live
steps.detail: Measured step: the GhostBuild Pi service reports camera frames. This step completes only when frames keep arriving (camera.frame_seq above 0) and the picture is not dark (camera.mean_luma above 25) for 1.5 s. 'Camera frame received' is MEASURED LIVE; 'scene visible' is only INFERRED from brightness. To see the camera yourself, the docs say rpicam-hello briefly displays a preview window containing the video feed from a connected camera.

faq.q: how do i see the camera

troubleshoot.why: A dark picture can mean the lens is covered; the docs mention a shipping film.

cites.quote: To remove it, gently peel it off.

troubleshoot.why: No new frames: the docs list the cable seating first.

cites.quote: Check that the FFC (Flat Flexible Cable) is firmly seated, fully inserted, and that the contacts face the correct direction.

troubleshoot.why: The docs also list updating to the latest software.

steps.title: Find the LED pin
steps.detail: Look at how YOUR LED is wired and write the GPIO (BCM) pin number in hardware/WIRING.md. GhostBuild never guesses the pin. The Raspberry Pi GPIO page uses GPIO17 only as a code example, not as a requirement.
warnings: Do not copy a pin number from an example; use the one actually wired.

steps.title: LED command test
steps.detail: Measured step, but only of the COMMAND: when the camera sees motion the Pi commands the LED on and reports led.commanded_on. That is COMMANDED, not measured light. Watch the LED with your own eyes. (PIVOT section 0A.)

faq.q: does this prove the led lit

troubleshoot.why: The command can succeed while the LED stays dark if the wiring differs from the configured pin.

cites.quote: A hand wave in the camera's field of view makes the Pi command the LED on
